issue.body:
## Bug

Nightly `0.12.7-nightly.202608241447` prints `can't find terminfo database` repeatedly in every TUI agent session. New TUI attaches fail, and already-running TUI sessions begin showing the same error after updating because the updated daemon attaches with the newly bundled tmux client.

**Source:** User report in an AO session on 2026-08-24 (no public chat URL available)  
**Analyzed against:** `ea895fa8b` (regression introduced by `c9a0adb21`, PR [#4293](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4293))  
**Observed artifact:** macOS arm64 desktop nightly `0.12.7-nightly.202608241447`  
**Confidence:** High  
**Priority:** P1 — TUI attachment is a core workflow and the packaged-app launch path has no practical in-app workaround.

## Reproduction

On macOS arm64 with the affected nightly installed:

1. Locate the staged bundled binary at `~/.ao/runtime/tmux/0.12.7-nightly.202608241447-darwin-arm64/tmux`.
2. Create an isolated session:
   ```sh
   BUNDLED_TMUX="$HOME/.ao/runtime/tmux/0.12.7-nightly.202608241447-darwin-arm64/tmux"
   "$BUNDLED_TMUX" -L ao-terminfo-repro -f /dev/null new-session -d -s triage 'sleep 30'
   ```
3. Attach using the same terminal arguments/environment as `Runtime.Attach`:
   ```sh
   TERM=xterm-256color "$BUNDLED_TMUX" -L ao-terminfo-repro -u -T RGB attach-session -t triage
   ```
4. Observe two lines of `can't find terminfo database`; the client exits with status 1.

`TERMINFO=/usr/share/terminfo` makes the same attach succeed, and `/usr/bin/infocmp xterm-256color` confirms the system entry exists.

## Root Cause

`frontend/scripts/build-tmux.mjs:136-158` builds a private static ncurses/libtinfo under a temporary CI prefix, then `frontend/scripts/build-tmux.mjs:184-190` statically links that library into tmux. The ncurses configuration does not specify portable system terminfo directories or embedded fallback entries.

The resulting shipped binary contains this compile-time database location:

```text
/Users/runner/work/agent-orchestrator/agent-orchestrator/.cache/bundled-tmux/darwin-arm64-r3-3.5a-2.1.12-stable-6.5-2.10.0/prefix/share/terminfo
```

That directory does not exist on an installed user's machine. Only the tmux executable and licenses are copied into `frontend/tmux`; no terminfo database is packaged.

`backend/internal/adapters/runtime/tmux/tmux.go:722-728` launches the bundled tmux client for every terminal attachment, and `attachEnv` at lines 768-788 forces `TERM=xterm-256color`. Initializing that terminal requires the missing database, so the error affects both new and pre-upgrade sessions whenever the nightly's client attaches.

The release smoke at `frontend/scripts/build-tmux.mjs:108-112` runs only `tmux -V`, which does not initialize terminal capabilities and therefore cannot catch this failure.

## Suggested Fix

- Make the bundled ncurses lookup portable, either by compiling the required terminal descriptions as ncurses fallbacks (at minimum `xterm-256color`) or by packaging a minimal terminfo tree and setting an AO-owned `TERMINFO` path for bundled tmux attaches. Do not retain the CI build prefix as the runtime default.
- Add an artifact smoke test that creates an isolated tmux server and performs a real PTY attach with `TERM=xterm-256color`; checking `tmux -V` alone is insufficient.
- Verify both macOS architectures and Linux release artifacts because the same build script produces all three.

## Impact

- TUI-mode agent sessions cannot be reliably attached in the affected nightly.
- Existing sessions regress immediately after update even though their agent processes were started before the update.
- The problem is harness-independent because it occurs in the tmux client before agent output is rendered.

## Related

- PR [#4293](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/4293) introduced the bundled tmux artifact and attachment path.
- PR [#2488](https://github.com/Untrivial-ai/agent-orchestrator/pull/2488) is the earlier open bundled-tmux implementation in the same subsystem.
